compiled_state.description:
## Summary

On 2026-09-01 (~12:00–16:00 PT) the Gerrit `LLM-Review` bot on host `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (`rebar-gerrit`) fail-closed every review: clones/materializations hit `No space left on device` on the 30 GiB root disk (reached 91–95% used), producing `VOTER_ERROR` / `coverage-gap (review-error)` vetoes. Change 2481 exhausted its retry budget to a fail-closed LLM-Review −1; 2479/2480/2482/2483 deferred. The host then wedged (SSM `ConnectionLost`, metrics feed stopped) because SSM/CloudWatch agents cannot spool to a full disk. Recovered by: EC2 reboot (cleared the wedge) + manual `docker builder prune -f` (no `--keep-storage`) + snapshot-store clear → 95% → 74%, bot healthy, reviews resumed, 2480 immediately re-reviewed +1.

This is a **defect escape**: the same fail-closed-on-full-disk class as closed 2731-4c53, 7a41-95f4, 3a52-2d79, 9bc0-1200, 28f9-535c, e2c5-f09b — all closed, yet it recurred.

## Evidence (on-box `docker system df`, 2026-09-01 ~16:05 PT, pre-prune)

- **Build Cache: 111 entries, 5.244 GB, 100% reclaimable** ← the dominant consumer.
- Images: 4, all ACTIVE, 2.802 GB, only 144 MB reclaimable → the 9bc0/2340 per-release image-retirement fix **is working** (no tagged-image pileup). Images were NOT the leak this time.
- Containers 3.572 GB; Local Volumes 947 MB; snapshot store `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots` only **1.4 GB**.

## Root cause — two confirmed structural gaps, neither about absolute disk size

**(1) The automated pressure-prune cannot reclaim the build-cache floor.**
`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:366 prune_docker_caches()` always runs `docker builder prune -f --keep-storage "$BUILD_CACHE_KEEP"` with `BUILD_CACHE_KEEP=5GB` (line 132) on **every** path — including the acute-pressure no-op-tick path (line 424). Today the cache was 5.244 GB, i.e. *at* the 5 GB keep floor, so the automated prune would have freed ~0. Recovery only worked because the manual prune omitted `--keep-storage`. This is the identical "reclaim runs, reports success, frees nothing" failure 9bc0 fixed for tagged images, now recurring for the build-cache floor. The `reclaim is not recovering the disk` marker (line 436) fires correctly but nothing escalates to a deeper reclaim. A 5 GB keep is 1/6 of a 30 GiB disk; combined with the active footprint (2.8 GB images + 3.57 GB containers + 0.95 GB volumes + OS + Gerrit data) the fixed baseline sits too close to full, and the snapshot janitor (which owns only the 1.4 GB snapshot store, and is enabled via `REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT=20`) mathematically cannot reach its 6 GB-free target because the deficit is held outside its pool.

**(2) The review clone/materialize hot path has no near-full admission control.**
`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py` + `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` abort on stall/throughput but never check free disk before cloning. So under pressure the bot keeps starting clones that ENOSPC mid-flight and fail-close as infra vetoes, instead of deferring cleanly until space is reclaimed.

## Decision needed (behavior change — escalated, do not implement without sign-off)

Two-part durable fix, grounded in prior art here and OSS practice:

**A. Acute-pressure emergency reclaim tier.** Keep the 5 GB steady-state keep for warm-build speed, but when root-disk used-% crosses a hard critical threshold (e.g. ≥90%, above the 80% soft `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`), escalate the pressure-prune to `docker builder prune -f` with keep→0 (and consider `docker image prune -af` guarded by the 9bc0 active-image protection). This mirrors kubelet's soft-vs-hard eviction thresholds and how CI runners (GitHub Actions, Buildkite, Zuul executors) aggressively GC BuildKit cache under disk pressure rather than retaining a fixed warm cache.

**B. Near-full admission control / backpressure in the review clone path.** Before materializing a snapshot, if free disk is below a hard floor, DEFER the review (retryable, vote-less per ADR 0069) instead of cloning into ENOSPC. This is standard executor practice (Zuul/Nodepool disk reservations, GitHub Actions pre-job free-space checks) and is the "prevent further filling when too close to full" backpressure that is currently missing.

**Recommendation: do both.** A alone still lets a review burst refill; B alone leaves the disk pinned. Explicitly NOT recommended: growing the EBS volume as the fix — the growth rate is workload-bound (~620 MiB/unique-tip review, 8386) and the watermark trigger is percentage-based, so a bigger disk only delays the identical wall. A temporary EBS bump is acceptable solely as a throwaway unwedge lever.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Under an induced acute-pressure condition (root ≥ critical threshold) with a build cache at/above the steady-state keep, the automated reclaim frees the excess cache (measured bytes freed > 0) and returns the disk below the soft threshold — verified by test/stub, not just an invocation marker (the 9bc0 lesson: measure effect, not calls).
2. When free disk is below the hard floor, the review path defers a new review (retryable, no vote posted) rather than starting a clone that ENOSPCs; verified by a unit/integration test simulating low free space.
3. Portability: the reclaim/admission logic must not depend on a specific CI provider (project.portability) — the free-space check is in-process/operation-linked.
4. No regression to warm-build steady-state behavior at normal disk levels.

## Provenance
Discovered during the 2026-09-01 review-bot outage triage. Related closed: 9bc0-1200, 28f9-535c, e2c5-f09b, 2731-4c53, 3a52-2d79, 7a41-95f4.
compiled_state.title: Disk-pressure reclaim cannot reach the build-cache floor under acute pressure, and the review clone path has no near-full admission control — review-bot fail-closes again
